title: Bleomycin-Induced Pulmonary Toxicity: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Incidence and Risk Factors
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Méta-analyse PRISMA 2020 (*Critical Reviews in Oncology/Hematology*, nov. 2026, IF 5,5, équipe de J. Gehl, 65 études / 7 601 patients) évaluant l'incidence et les facteurs de risque de toxicité pulmonaire à la bléomycine IV : contrairement aux cures répétées de chimiothérapie systémique (incidence globale 18 % en oncologie médicale), l'injection unique ou pauciséquentielle d'ECT à faible dose cumulative reste dépourvue de surrisque lié à l'âge ou aux métastases pulmonaires.

[ABSTRACT EN] Bleomycin remains an important component of curative regimens for malignancies such as germ cell tumors, Hodgkin lymphoma, and in the local treatment modality electrochemotherapy. A limiting toxicity is bleomycin-induced pulmonary toxicity (BIP), with considerable variance in reported incidence across studies. OBJECTIVE: To estimate the incidence of BIP after intravenous bleomycin treatment and investigate the influence of diagnostic definitions, patient characteristics, and treatment-related factors on reported incidence. METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted according to PRISMA 2020. MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane Library were searched through May 2026. Studies including patients aged ≥15 years treated with intravenous bleomycin were eligible. Risk of bias was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist for Prevalence Studies. Random-effects meta-analysis and prespecified subgroup analyses were performed. RESULTS: A total of 65 studies comprising 7601 patients were included. The pooled incidence of BIP was 18% (95% CI 15-21%) with substantial between-study heterogeneity (I(2) = 87.3%). Reported incidence varied by diagnostic definition, ranging from 42% in imaging-based studies to 16% in studies using symptom-based composite definitions. Diagnostic definition explained a substantial proportion of between-study heterogeneity (R(2)=28%). No significant study-level associations were found between reported BIP incidence and age, sex, year of publication, overall cumulative bleomycin dose, use of granulocyte colony-stimulating factor, smoking history, or lung metastases. CONCLUSIONS: Reported BIP incidence varies widely, largely due to differences in diagnostic definitions. Standardized, clinically meaningful diagnostic criteria are needed to improve comparability between studies and support evidence-based clinical decision-making. REGISTRATION: PROSPERO (CRDxxxxxxxxxx).

title: Quantitative imaging-pathology correlation in nodular fasciitis and diagnostic discrimination from sarcoma
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude rétrospective sur 261 patients (*Insights into Imaging*, nov. 2026 : 128 fasciites nodulaires et 133 sarcomes des tissus mous en IRM 3T) démontrant que l'ADC moyen et le signe de la queue fasciale combinés aux biomarqueurs histopathologiques distinguent fasciite nodulaire et sarcome avec une AUC de 0,96.

[ABSTRACT EN] Objectives To investigate associations between key magnetic resonance imaging features of nodular fasciitis (NF) and quantitative histopathologic biomarkers, and to evaluate whether their integration provides complementary information for differentiating NF from soft tissue sarcoma (STS) in diagnostically equivocal settings. Materials and methods This retrospective study included 128 patients with NF and 133 with STS who underwent preoperative 3-T MRI between May 2023 and June 2025. Two blinded musculoskeletal radiologists independently evaluated predefined imaging features, including fascial tail sign, T2 heterogeneity score, enhancement pattern, perilesional edema, and mean/minimum apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC). Histopathology quantified cellular density, collagen content, and myxoid degeneration. Imaging-pathology correlations were assessed using Spearman analysis and multivariable regression. Diagnostic performance of MRI-only, pathology-only, and combined models was evaluated using logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic (ROC), area under the curve (AUC) analysis, calibration, decision curve analysis, and bootstrap validation. Results T2 heterogeneity correlated positively with myxoid degeneration (ρ = 0.52) and negatively with collagen content (ρ = -0.28) (p Conclusion Imaging features of NF were associated with underlying stromal and cellular substrates. Integrating imaging features with quantitative pathology biomarkers may support radiology-pathology concordance assessment in selected diagnostically equivocal cases. Key points Question How can we improve radiology-pathology concordance and reduce interpretative variability for NF cases presenting with suspicious, diagnostically equivocal magnetic resonance imaging findings? Findings T2 heterogeneity and diffusion measurements are associated with stromal composition and cellularity, while predefined MRI features demonstrated substantial-to-excellent inter-reader agreement. Critical relevance statement Embedding explicit AHA criteria in the prompt let an 8B model approach 671B-model agreement (38.91-81.52%), supporting standardized text-based workflows without fine-tuning.

title: Short-term clinical and imaging outcomes after ultrasound-guided cooled radiofrequency ablation for advanced knee osteoarthritis: a retrospective cohort study
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude de cohorte (*Pain Management*, nov. 2026, 31 patients / 35 genoux, 91 % de gonarthrose sévère Kellgren-Lawrence 3–4) démontrant une baisse significative des douleurs (marche, repos, nuit) et une diminution de la synovite en IRM (Hoffa-synovitis / effusion-synovitis) sans aggravation des lésions osseuses sous-chondrales (BML) ni de l'arthrose à 3 mois.

[ABSTRACT EN] OBJECTIVE: To evaluate short-term clinical and imaging outcomes after ultrasound-guided cooled radiofrequency ablation (CRFA) in patients predominantly with advanced knee osteoarthritis (KOA). METHODS: This retrospective cohort analysis included prospectively recorded data from 31 patients (35 knees; age, 73.6 ± 8.8 years; Kellgren-Lawrence [KL] grade 3 or 4 in 91%). Outcomes at baseline and 3 months included visual analog scale (VAS) pain, Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (KOOS), KL grade, mechanical axis percentage, and MRI Osteoarthritis Knee Score assessments of bone marrow lesions (BMLs), Hoffa-synovitis, and effusion-synovitis. Sensitivity analysis retained the first-treated knee in bilateral cases. RESULTS: VAS changes were -9.3 for rest pain, -24.0 for walking pain, and -15.0 for night pain (all p < 0.05). Walking VAS decreased by at least 30% in 65.7% and by at least 50% in 42.9% of knees. Four KOOS subscales improved, including KOOS Pain by 12.8 points (p < 0.001). No significant group-level changes were observed in KL grade, alignment, or BML scores. Hoffa-synovitis and effusion-synovitis scores decreased. No serious procedure-related adverse events were documented. CONCLUSION: CRFA was associated with improved pain and function at 3 months without group-level worsening in KL grade, alignment, or BML scores. Longer-term controlled studies are required.

title: Evolving role of cryoablation and cryoneurolysis for interventional pain management
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Mise au point de référence publiée dans *European Radiology* (nov. 2026, IF 4,7, équipe de D. Filippiadis) structurant les indications, le mécanisme d'axonotmésis réversible (classification de Sunderland II) et les protocoles de cryoablation tumorale (ostéome ostéoïde, métastases osseuses, tumeurs des parties molles) et de cryoneurolyse périphérique (nerfs intercostaux, clunéaux, géniculés, névrome de Morton).

[ABSTRACT EN] Despite advances in pain management, pain remains a major global health challenge in both oncological and non-oncological patients. Long-term pharmacological treatment is often restricted by insufficient therapeutic benefit and adverse events, highlighting the need for alternative approaches such as image-guided pain therapies. The idea of treating pain with cold has been recognized for centuries, and today cryotherapy has emerged as a valuable minimally invasive option for pain management. Cryoablation refers to the destruction of tissue with extreme cold and has an increasing role, especially in the treatment of benign (e.g., osteoid osteoma), malignant bone (i.e., metastases), and soft tissue tumors, either with a curative or palliative intent. Cryoneurolysis is a related but distinct application, focusing either on peripheral nerve modulation or nerve destruction. Cryoneurolysis may be highly effective for the treatment of acute or chronic pain, including sympathetic neurolysis in cancer and non-cancer-related pain syndromes. The general approach in patients with tumor-related pain depends on whether the lesion itself can be ablated or not. In non-oncologic patients, cryoneurolysis of the responsible nerve is typically performed following a positive response to a diagnostic nerve block. Potential indications for cryotherapy are constantly evolving; however, evidence, especially for cryoneurolysis, is still limited and based mostly on single-center case series and retrospective studies. Standardized ablation protocols are lacking, and for the duration of cycles, most experts rely on imaging visualization and validated protocols. Equally important, successful integration of cryoablation and cryoneurolysis into daily practice requires structured workflows across different patient pathways and interdisciplinary management. KEY POINTS: Question Pain management remains a major global health challenge and an unmet need in oncological and non-oncological patients. Findings Cryotherapy, in terms of cryoablation and cryoneurolysis, is increasingly incorporated in multimodal curative and palliative pain care concepts, for treatment of acute and chronic pain syndromes. Clinical relevance Advancement and validation of standardized treatment protocols are needed to strengthen evidence and further enhance clinical implementation in interventional radiology practice and interdisciplinary patient care.

title: Pudendal Neuralgia in a Tertiary Pain Clinic: Presentation, Treatment, and Factors Associated with Neuromodulation in 224 Adults
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude de cohorte sur 224 adultes (*Pain and Therapy*, nov. 2026, IF 3,8) évaluant le parcours interventionnel de la névralgie pudendale : bloc pudendal diagnostique réalisé chez 59,4 % des patients et radiofréquence pulsée (PRF) chez 28,6 %, avec identification d'un bloc diagnostique positif (OR ajusté = 4,88) et d'une étiologie post-chirurgicale confirmée (OR = 2,83) comme facteurs prédictifs majeurs de réponse aux thérapies de neuromodulation.

[ABSTRACT EN] INTRODUCTION: Pudendal neuralgia is an under-recognized cause of chronic, disabling neuropathic perineal pain affecting both women and men. Real-world data on its presentation, its treatment within a specialty pain service, and the factors that accompany escalation to interventional therapy are scarce. We hypothesized that an iatrogenic (postsurgical) origin and relief after a diagnostic pudendal nerve block would identify the patients who reach neuromodulation. METHODS: We performed a retrospective manual review of the complete electronic records of all adults with documented pudendal neuralgia, pudendal neuropathy, or pudendal nerve entrapment managed at a single tertiary pain clinic between 2009 and 2026. Demographics, clinical presentation, presumed etiology, treatments, and outcomes were abstracted from the free-text record. Ascertainment was in two stages: variables were first identified by structured text screening of the free-text record, and the two variables most susceptible to false-positive screening, a postsurgical etiology and receipt of neuromodulation, were then verified against the source charts by manual review of every screen-positive record. The chart-verified definitions are used throughout. Associations between binary variables were tested by the chi-squared test, with odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI); factors associated with neuromodulation were assessed by multivariable logistic regression. RESULTS: Among 224 patients (138 women [61.6%], 86 men [38.4%]; median age 48.5 years, interquartile range 35-64), pain was worse when sitting in 57.6% and burning in 39.3%, and involvement was bilateral in 21.9%. Text screening identified a possible postsurgical onset in 46.4%, but chart re-adjudication confirmed a named operation preceding the pain in only 31 patients (13.8%), of whom 6 had undergone a clearly non-pelvic procedure; confirmed postsurgical onset was therefore less frequent than documented entrapment features (24.1%) and comparable to childbirth (15.9% of women). Care was heavily interventional: 59.4% received a pudendal nerve block, 28.6% pulsed radiofrequency, and 9.4% underwent surgical decompression. Neuromodulation was documented in the record of 64 patients (28.6%), but an electrode was placed in only 26 (11.6%) and a permanent device implanted in 18 (8.0%): spinal cord stimulation in 14, sacral neuromodulation in 2, dorsal root ganglion stimulation in 1, and pudendal nerve stimulation in 1. Three factors were independently associated with documented neuromodulation: relief after a diagnostic block (adjusted OR 4.88, 95% CI 1.91-12.46%), a refractory course (2.92, 1.52-5.60%), and chart-confirmed postsurgical onset (2.83, 1.17-6.82%); c-statistic 0.76. In an exploratory model restricted to the 18 implanted patients, a refractory course (7.40, 1.98-27.61%) and postsurgical onset (4.24, 1.29-13.94%) remained associated with the outcome whereas relief after a block did not (5.90, 0.72-48.31%). CONCLUSIONS: In routine pain-clinic practice, pudendal neuralgia is managed along an interventional pathway, but device implantation is considerably less common than the frequency with which neuromodulation is discussed. A confirmed postsurgical onset is less common than text screening suggests, yet is disproportionately associated with escalation. Being observational, these findings describe how care proceeds rather than establishing cause.

title: Intraarticular acetabular osteoid osteoma treated with CT-guided radiofrequency ablation after unsuccessful arthroscopy: a case report and literature review
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Publication d'octobre 2026 (*Skeletal Radiology*) illustrant le traitement curatif par radiofréquence sous scanner d'un ostéome ostéoïde intra-articulaire de la fosse acétabulaire après échec d'une résection arthroscopique, avec disparition complète de la synovite réactionnelle et des douleurs.

[ABSTRACT EN] Acetabular osteoid osteoma is uncommon, and treatment can be difficult when the lesion is intraarticular or associated with osteoarthritis. We report a 17-year-old male with an intraarticular acetabular osteoid osteoma. The lesion was located in the medial portion of the acetabular fossa and was associated with synovitis, joint effusion, joint space narrowing, and osteophyte formation. Arthroscopy was initially selected for lesion resection and joint assessment. However, the medial location limited instrument access, preventing complete resection. The residual lesion was subsequently treated with CT-guided radiofrequency ablation (RFA) using a posterior osseous trajectory and intraarticular cooling with chilled 5% dextrose solution. At 4 weeks, hip pain had completely resolved, and MRI showed resolution of perilesional bone marrow edema. Pain relief persisted through 12 months without analgesic use. A literature review summarizes previous treatment approaches for acetabular osteoid osteoma. This case illustrates that treatment planning should account for lesion location, joint condition, and technical feasibility. CT-guided RFA may be useful when a safe percutaneous trajectory to the lesion can be planned.

title: Management of sacral fragility fractures leading to spinopelvic dissociation: a scoping review
container-title: European journal of orthopaedic surgery & traumatology : orthopedie traumatologie
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Revue systématique PRISMA-ScR (*Eur J Orthop Surg Traumatol*, oct. 2026, 8 études / 235 patients) consacrée aux fractures bilatérales postérieures du sacrum par insuffisance osseuse (fractures en H/U et Rommens IVb), confirmant que le vissage percutané est la technique de référence après échec du traitement médical pour restaurer la mobilité et soulager la douleur.

[ABSTRACT EN] Purpose Fragility fractures affecting the sacrum present an increasing challenge to orthopaedic practice, due to limited comparative data and the absence of consensus on optimal management. U-Type and Rommens Type IVb fractures may result in a bilateral pattern of spinopelvic dissociation with possible neurological injury. This scoping review aims to summarise the current principles of care, indications for surgery, and outcomes of operative versus non-operative treatment for low-energy bilateral posterior sacral fractures (BPSFs). Methods This scoping review adhered to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). A systematic search of electronic databases identified studies including ≥ 10 patients with Bilateral Posterior Sacral Fractures (BPSFs) comparing operative and non-operative approaches. Two reviewers independently screened titles, abstracts, and full texts against predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, resolving disagreements by consensus. Data were extracted using a standardised form and summarised narratively with reference to mobility, quality of life, and patient-reported outcome measures. From 421 studies screened, eight met inclusion criteria. Results From 421 screened records, eight studies including 235 patients met inclusion criteria. Operative management resulted from failed non-operative care in most cases. Percutaneous screw fixation was the most common surgical technique utilised. Although one study reported improved outcomes with early fixation, considerable heterogeneity in surgical approach and timing was observed with a similar lack of consensus on non-operative regimes and their point of 'failure'. Conclusion Operative management may enhance pain relief, mobility, and function in selected patients with BPSFs, though with notable implant-related risks. Careful patient selection remains key, and further prospective studies are needed to establish optimal non-operative management and those who would benefit from early operative intervention.

title: Photodynamic Bone Stabilization in Pathologic Humeral Fractures: Implant Safety, Pain Relief and Functional Outcomes
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude bicentrique sur données prospectives (*Cancers*, oct. 2026, IF 4,5, Open-Access) portant sur 51 patients métastatiques (52 fractures humérales avérées ou menaçantes Mirels 8–10) traités par ballonnet centromédullaire photopolymérisable mini-invasif (IlluminOss®) : chute rapide de la douleur (NRS de 7,1 à 2,0, p < 0,001), doublement du score fonctionnel MSTS-UE (de 9,5 à 20/30, p < 0,001), implant radiotransparent sans artefact TDM/IRM et faible taux de défaillance mécanique (7,7 %).

[ABSTRACT EN] Background: Pathologic fractures of the humerus due to metastatic disease cause severe pain, loss of function and reduced quality of life. Surgical treatment is predominantly palliative and aims to achieve rapid pain relief, early functional recovery and minimal treatment-related morbidity. The photodynamic bone stabilization system (IlluminOss ® ) is a minimally invasive, radiolucent, intramedullary device that may address these needs. Methods: This retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data from two centers included 51 patients with 52 pathologic humeral lesions (completed or impending fractures) treated with photodynamic intramedullary stabilization between 2013 and 2025. Baseline variables comprised demographics, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status, comorbidities, pain (numeric rating scale, NRS) and function (Musculoskeletal Tumor Society Upper Extremity Score, MSTS-UE; Toronto Extremity Salvage Score, TESS). Lesion characteristics, operative details, in-hospital course, follow-up outcomes (TESS, patient satisfaction/quality of life) and long-term endpoints (survival, complications) were recorded. Results: The study cohort (25 women, 26 men; mean age 68.5 years) represented a highly palliative population with advanced, disseminated malignant disease. Of the 52 humeral lesions, 35 (67.3%) presented as pathological fractures, whereas 17 lesions (32.7%) were classified as impending fractures due to extensive osteolysis. Among the impending fractures, Mirels scores ranged from 8 to 10, with three lesions scoring 8, eight lesions scoring 9, and six lesions scoring 10. ECOG performance status was 0-2 in 75.0% and 3-4 in 25.0% of patients. Preoperative pain was high (mean NRS 7.1) and function markedly reduced (median MSTS-UE 9.5/30; median TESS 36.5/100). Postoperatively, pain improved significantly from NRS 7.1 to 2.0 ( p p p n = 44) demonstrated a median survival of 6 months for ECOG 0-2 and 3 months for ECOG 3-4. Implant failure (Henderson type III) occurred four times (7.7%) and was successfully revised with plate and/or screw osteosynthesis or diaphyseal replacement. Conclusions: Photodynamic intramedullary stabilization provides effective treatment for selected pathologic humeral lesions with low implant failure rate, offering rapid pain relief, functional improvement and low perioperative morbidity. Implant failure in complex fracture morphologies highlights the need for morphology-adapted indication and consideration of supplemental fixation in high-risk cases.

title: Image-Guided Ablative Options for Desmoid Fibromatosis: Contemporary Evidence and Guideline Integration
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Mise au point de référence (*Curr Treat Options Oncol*, oct. 2026) détaillant l'intégration de la cryoablation percutanée dans l'algorithme multidisciplinaire des tumeurs desmoïdes symptomatiques ou progressives, incluant les stratégies d'ablation subtotale délibérée à proximité des nerfs critiques.

[ABSTRACT EN] Opinion statement Most patients with a newly diagnosed desmoid tumor should begin with multidisciplinary evaluation and active surveillance rather than immediate intervention, provided that symptoms are limited and further growth is unlikely to create irreversible morbidity. Treatment should be initiated when pain, functional limitation, sustained progression, or threatened critical structures make continued observation unacceptable. Percutaneous cryoablation is generally favored because the ice ball can be monitored directly, treatment can be personalized/tailored with the synergistic benefit of multiple probes, and the procedure can be repeated or staged when a complete margin would be unsafe. Complete ablation should be targeted when the entire tumor can be covered without jeopardizing skin, nerves, bowel, or other vulnerable structures; deliberate subtotal ablation is appropriate when the principal goal is pain relief or functional improvement and a safe circumferential margin is not achievable. Hydrodissection, skin warming, neural protection, and conservative treatment near critical anatomy are essential. Magnetic resonance-guided focused ultrasound is an attractive incisionless alternative for tumors with a favorable acoustic window. Microwave or radiofrequency ablation should be reserved for carefully selected lesions and experienced operators; electrochemotherapy and chemical ablation remain investigational with some promising early evidence. Embolization can be useful for hypervascular tumors that are poorly suited to direct percutaneous treatment. Local and systemic therapy should not be viewed as mutually exclusive: systemic treatment is often preferable for diffuse, intra-abdominal, or anatomically hazardous disease, while ablation can address a dominant symptomatic focus, residual viable tumor, or focal progression. Further study into the benefits and sequencing of combining local therapy with systemic or targeted options will be helpful in the multi-disciplinary evaluation of this complex patient cohort.

title: Accuracy of preoperative biopsy in identifying definitive histology in malignant chondroid tumors
container-title: European journal of surgical oncology : the journal of the European Society of Surgical Oncology and the British Association of Surgical Oncology
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude rétrospective sur 111 chondrosarcomes opérés (*European Journal of Surgical Oncology*, oct. 2026) évaluant la concordance de grade entre la biopsie percutanée préopératoire au trocart (CNB) et la pièce de résection : concordance parfaite (100 %) pour les chondrosarcomes dédifférenciés, mais risque élevé de sous-évaluation dans les grades G1–G2 (concordance globale 48 %), imposant un ciblage biopsique guidé par l'IRM sur les zones d'ostéolyse ou d'envahissement des parties molles.

[ABSTRACT EN] Introduction The reliability of Core Needle Biopsy (CNB) for the preoperative diagnosis of chondroid tumors and for determining the histological grade of chondrosarcoma (CS) remains debated. The aim of the study was to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy and agreement of CNB in determining the histological grade of CS. Materials and methods A retrospective study was conducted including all patients who underwent surgical resection for CS at a tertiary research hospital between 2006 and 2023. All the included patients had preoperative histological diagnosis obtained by CNB. All samples were evaluated by experienced musculoskeletal pathologists. The agreement between CNB and definitive histology was assessed using Cohen's Kappa (κ). Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS version 29. Results A total of 111 patients with a mean age of 54.5 ± 16 years were included. Overall concordance between CNB and final histology was observed in 53/111 cases, corresponding to a concordace of 48%. Among the 58 discordant cases, 13 (22.4%) showed a discrepancy of two or more histological grades. Based on the biopsy grade, the concordance was 0% (0/4) for chondroma, 46% (29/63) for G1, 41.4% (12/29) for G2, 40% (2/5) for G3, and 100% (10/10) for dedifferentiated tumors (κ = 0.28). Based on anatomical location, it was stratified by hemipelvis (31 cases, κ = 0.3), distal femur (14, κ = 0.5), proximal femur (19, κ = 0.1), proximal humerus (8, κ = 0), scapula (8, κ = 0.6), and proximal tibia (11, κ = 0.18). Conclusion This study showed modest agreement between the histological grade obtained by CNB and the definitive postoperative grade in CS. Agreement was higher in dedifferentiated tumors, in central skeletal lesions, and in tumors with soft tissue invasion. Conversely, concordance was particularly poor in G1-G2 CSs and in peripheral lesions, with an increased risk of undergrading.

title: Multimodal imaging and artificial intelligence for bone tumor diagnosis: Comparative performance and emerging technologies
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Revue critique publiée dans le *Journal of Bone Oncology* (oct./déc. 2026, IF 3,4) démontrant que la limite principale des modèles diagnostiques en oncologie osseuse réside dans la variabilité du standard histologique : la concordance de grade entre biopsie au trocart (CNB) et pièce opératoire dans les chondrosarcomes centraux chute de κ = 0,63 sur les os longs à κ = 0,12 dans le bassin.

[ABSTRACT EN] Multimodal imaging is central to the diagnosis, staging, and management of bone tumors. Radiography and computed tomography remain essential for initial assessment and cortical evaluation, magnetic resonance imaging provides superior soft tissue contrast and local staging accuracy, and positron emission tomography enhances detection of metastatic disease and treatment response. No single technique suffices across clinical scenarios. Advances in artificial intelligence and radiomics offer avenues to augment this framework, with demonstrated potential in lesion classification, segmentation, prognostication, and response prediction. This review advances a specific argument rather than surveying available technologies: that the principal constraint on artificial intelligence in musculoskeletal oncology is the stability of the reference standard rather than algorithmic capability. Ground truth in bone tumors is unstable on four grounds. Core needle biopsy samples a limited volume and may miss the highest-grade component: agreement between biopsy and resection grade in central chondrosarcoma falls from a weighted kappa of 0.63 in long bones to 0.12 in the pelvis. Expert interpretation is itself inconsistent, with interobserver kappa for grading cartilaginous tumors of 0.44 among musculoskeletal pathologists and 0.35 among radiologists. Molecular criteria have redefined entities within the past decade, so older datasets contain classes that no longer exist as defined. And histological classification does not reliably predict clinical behavior. Consequently, measurable accuracy has a ceiling set by the reference standard rather than the algorithm, and apparent failure on external validation may reflect label divergence between institutions rather than model deficiency. Evidence is graded throughout, and clinical readiness distinguished from technical performance. No system for primary bone tumor characterization has regulatory clearance in the United States or Europe, and formal appraisal of this literature confirms low methodological compliance and infrequent external validation. Progress will depend on multicenter validation and protocol harmonization, and, distinctively for this field, on composite reference standards, outcome-based endpoints, and explicit uncertainty modelling, since ground-truth instability can be mitigated but not eliminated.

title: Diagnostic performance of computed tomography-guided percutaneous bone biopsy in musculoskeletal oncology: A single-center cohort study
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude de cohorte monocentrique (*World Journal of Radiology*, oct. 2026, IF 2,5, Open-Access) portant sur 64 biopsies osseuses percutanées consécutives guidées par scanner : rendement diagnostique de 93,75 % (60/64) dès le premier prélèvement, concordance histologique de 100 % parmi les prélèvements contributifs, révision du diagnostic clinique pré-geste dans 9,4 % des cas (6/64) et 0 % de complication majeure SIR.

[ABSTRACT EN] Background Computed tomography guided percutaneous bone biopsy provides tissue for the assessment of suspected primary and secondary bone lesions. Diagnostic yield, concordance with subsequent diagnostic assessment, and adverse events describe different aspects of performance. Their interpretation depends on case selection, outcome definitions, and the completeness and independence of diagnostic verification. Aim To describe diagnostic yield, recorded diagnostic concordance, and complications in a retrospective single-center cohort of image-guided bone biopsies. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 64 consecutive image-guided percutaneous bone biopsy procedures performed from January 2023 through December 2025. Diagnostic yield required clinically useful histopathology without repeat sampling. Recorded concordance used a composite of surgical histopathology, immunohistochemistry-supported assessment, or clinical and imaging follow-up. Non-diagnostic procedures remained in the full-cohort analysis. Complications were classified using the legacy Society of Interventional Radiology system. Proportions were summarized with exact binomial 95% confidence intervals (CI); no external hypothesis tests were performed. Results Diagnostic yield was 60/64 (93.75%; 95%CI: 84.8%-98.3%). Recorded concordance among 60 diagnostic, evaluable procedures was 60/60 (100%; 95%CI: 94.0%-100%). The full-cohort concordant diagnostic-result rate was 60/64 (93.75%) when four non-diagnostic procedures were counted as failures. Six biopsies revised the pre-procedural clinical diagnosis. Pelvic lesions were the most frequent sites. Two minor class B biopsy-tract fistulas occurred (2/64, 3.1%; 95%CI: 0.4%-10.8%); no major complications were recorded (0/64; 95%CI: 0%-5.6%). The heterogeneous cohort, incomplete verification reporting, and potentially non-independent composite reference standard limit interpretation of the conditional concordance estimate. Conclusion This cohort showed high diagnostic yield and two recorded minor complications. Conditional concordance does not establish unbiased diagnostic accuracy; independent verification and prospective confirmation are needed.

title: Current Role of Radiomics for Management of Soft Tissue Sarcoma
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Revue de synthèse (*Current Treatment Options in Oncology*, oct. 2026, IF 4,1) faisant le point sur l'apport des biomarqueurs radiomiques extraits de l'IRM conventionnelle dans les sarcomes des tissus mous : discrimination bas grade vs haut grade avant biopsie, prédiction précoce de la nécrose post-traitement néoadjuvant et stratification pronostique du risque métastatique.

[ABSTRACT EN] Opinion statement Soft tissue sarcomas represent a diverse set of malignancies with equally diverse behavior, ranging from relatively indolent low-grade tumors to aggressive high-grade tumors with high metastatic potential. Initial diagnosis hinges on tissue biopsy for determining histologic subtype and grade, while conventional imaging plays critical roles in defining local tumor size and extent, staging, treatment response, and disease surveillance. However, conventional semantic interpretation of imaging studies overlooks much of the complex imaging data embedded in routine clinical studies. Radiomics encompasses the identification of novel disease biomarkers extracted from highly quantitative characterizations of tumor structure and heterogeneity and has shown promise in providing a deeper understanding of soft tissue sarcomas. Given the increasing usage of imaging in soft tissue sarcomas, particularly usage of MRI, it behooves both clinicians and radiologists to further the depth of understanding that may be gleaned from radiomics. These insights, although primarily experimental, represent a rapidly evolving landscape in soft tissue sarcoma diagnosis and management where radiomics will be increasingly integrated into clinical practice. The present work focuses on the latest updates with regards to the application of radiomics to the diagnosis, prediction of treatment response, assessment of treatment response, and prognosis of soft tissue sarcomas and how they may affect sarcoma management.

title: Intraoperative Neurophysiological Monitoring During Continuous Radiofrequency Treatment of Morton's Neuroma: Complete Ablation
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Série prospective de 22 patients / 30 névromes de Morton (*Medicina*, oct. 2026) traités par radiofréquence continue échoguidée sous monitorage en temps réel des potentiels d'action nerveux sensitifs (SNAP), obtenant 86,7 % de succès global (96,3 % hors métatarsalgie mécanique) et 100 % de succès en rattrapage après échec d'une RF antérieure.

[ABSTRACT EN] Background and Objectives : Morton's neuroma is a compressive neuropathy of the common plantar digital nerve that most frequently affects the third intermetatarsal space. Continuous radiofrequency (RF) ablation has reported success rates of approximately 80-85%; however, recent histological evidence suggests that RF does not consistently achieve complete neural ablation. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring of sensory nerve action potentials (SNAPs) to optimize the outcomes of continuous RF ablation in the treatment of Morton's neuroma. Materials and Methods : This prospective case series included 22 patients (30 neuromas) treated with ultrasound-guided continuous RF ablation combined with intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring. SNAPs were recorded before, during, and after each RF application until complete abolition of sensory nerve conduction was confirmed. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), the Foot Function Index (FFI), and the Giannini Interdigital Neuroma Clinical Evaluation Score at 3, 6, and 12 months postoperatively. Results : At the 12-month follow-up, satisfactory outcomes (Giannini score ≥60) were achieved in 86.7% of neuromas (26/30). The mean VAS pain score decreased from 8.67 preoperatively to 1.67 at 12 months. Among the seven neuromas with previous unsuccessful RF treatment, all achieved satisfactory outcomes following the monitored procedure. The four cases with poor outcomes were predominantly associated with a positive anesthetic suppression test, suggesting concomitant mechanical metatarsalgia rather than treatment failure. After excluding cases with likely diagnostic misclassification, the adjusted success rate increased to 96.3%. Conclusions : Intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring enables real-time confirmation of complete sensory nerve ablation during continuous RF treatment. Its main potential value appears to lie in patients with previous unsuccessful conventional RF, all of whom achieved satisfactory outcomes in this series. Persistent postoperative symptoms appeared to be more closely related to concomitant forefoot pathology than to technical limitations of the RF procedure.

title: Percutaneous cryoablation of musculoskeletal tumours: the largest reported single-centre case series - outcomes, complications and subgroup analysis
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Série monocentrique de référence (*Skeletal Radiology*, oct. 2026, équipe de R. Botchu, 48 patients) évaluant la cryoablation percutanée des tumeurs musculo-squelettiques (métastases, tumeurs cartilagineuses et tumeurs osseuses primitives/bénignes), avec 73 % de réponse clinique (58 % complète/bonne, 15 % partielle), une baisse de densité TDM (UH) dans 94 % des cas et aucune complication majeure CIRSE.

[ABSTRACT EN] Objectives Cryoablation is an image-guided, minimally invasive treatment technique that uses extreme cold to induce tumour destruction. Its role in musculoskeletal oncology has expanded in recent years, although large clinical series remain limited. This study reports a large single-centre experience of percutaneous cryoablation for musculoskeletal tumours, including metastatic lesions, benign and cartilaginous tumours, and primary bone tumours. Materials and methods This was a single-centre retrospective cohort study conducted at a tertiary musculoskeletal oncology centre. All procedures were performed by a single specialist musculoskeletal interventional radiologist with over 20 years of experience. The study included patients who underwent percutaneous cryoablation for musculoskeletal tumours between June 2021 and December 2025. Clinical response, radiological response, recurrence, and complications were assessed over a median follow-up of 3 months (mean 8.7 months; range 0-48 months). Radiological response was assessed using pre-treatment and post-treatment Hounsfield Unit (HU) measurements on CT; this is not a validated radiological scoring system and is reported as a complementary, exploratory marker alongside standard clinical response assessment. Complications were graded using the CIRSE classification system. Results A total of 48 patients underwent percutaneous cryoablation during the study period. The cohort included 26 males and 22 females, with a median age of 40 years. A good or complete response was achieved in 28 patients, representing 58% of the total cohort. A partial response was achieved in seven patients, representing 15% of the total cohort. HU reduction was observed in 45 of 48 patients, representing 94% of the cohort. The overall complication rate was 6.3%, with three complications recorded among 48 procedures. No major complications or procedure-related deaths were observed. Conclusions Cryoablation appears to be a safe and effective minimally invasive treatment for selected musculoskeletal tumours. Most patients achieved a good, complete, or partial response, with a low complication rate. Hounsfield Unit reduction after treatment may provide a useful, though as yet non-validated, marker of radiological response. Further prospective studies with longer follow-up, standardised response criteria and validated complication grading are needed to confirm these findings.

title: Complications of vertebral augmentation in metastatic spinal fractures: a systematic review of multiple study designs
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Revue systématique d'envergure (*Journal of Bone Oncology*, sept. 2026, 76 études, 3 234 patients, ≥ 5 737 vertèbres traitées) quantifiant précisément le taux de complications symptomatiques (3,41 %) et de fuites de ciment (20,7 %, majoritairement asymptomatiques) lors de la cimentoplastie des métastases rachidiennes.

[ABSTRACT EN] Background Vertebral augmentation techniques, including vertebroplasty and kyphoplasty, are widely used to relieve pain and restore spinal stability in patients with metastatic vertebral lesions. Despite their widespread use, the full spectrum and clinical significance of procedure-related complications remain incompletely characterised. This systematic review aims to summarise and characterise all reported complications associated with vertebral augmentation for metastatic thoracolumbar disease. Methods A comprehensive search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science databases was performed. Studies reporting complications associated with vertebral augmentation procedures for metastatic thoracolumbar spinal fractures were included. Randomised controlled trials, observational studies, case series, and case reports were eligible. Due to substantial heterogeneity across studies, a descriptive synthesis was performed. Results A total of 76 studies were included, comprising 3234 patients and at least 5737 vertebral levels treated. The overall weighted complication rate was 25.5%, while the weighted rate of symptomatic complications was 3.41%. Cement leakage was the most frequently reported complication, with a weighted mean incidence of 20.7%, although the majority were asymptomatic. Other complications included postprocedural pain (1.77%), pulmonary cement embolism (1.08%), and adjacent level fractures (0.79%). Studies using CT imaging reported significantly higher cement leakage rates (28.6% vs 11.9%, p = 0.004). Case reports described rare but potentially severe complications, including needle-tract tumour seeding, tumour extrusion, and cement migration to cardiac structures. Conclusions This review presents a comprehensive and detailed description of all complications of vertebral augmentation for treatment of metastatic spine disease and reinforce its safety. Differences in imaging protocols and reporting standards contribute to variability in reported complication rates. Further prospective studies with standardised complication reporting are needed.

title: Iliosacral Screw Fixation for Treating Sacral Fractures: A Modified Pedicle-Guided Fixation Technique in Prone Position
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Série clinique (*Orthopaedic Surgery*, sept./nov. 2026, PMC Open-Access, 22 patients) décrivant une technique modifiée de vissage ilio-sacré percutané en procubitus guidée par les repères du pédicule de S1 : taux d'excellence de positionnement intra-osseux au scanner de 97 %, absence totale de complication radiculaire et amélioration significative de l'EVA douleur et du score fonctionnel de Majeed.

[ABSTRACT EN] Background Sacral fractures are posterior pelvic ring injuries which mechanisms range from high-energy trauma to low-energy falls in osteoporotic patients. In surgical treatment, percutaneous approaches have demonstrated significant shorter operation time and less soft tissue damage. In this study, we present a method of iliosacral (SI) screw insertion in prone position, with modified pedicle-guided technique. Methods The present study is a retrospective case series of 22 patients for SI screw fixation from February 2019 to September 2023 under our method. Surgical technique was described in detail with images. Perioperative clinical parameters were analyzed. Activity status, complications, data of 10-point visual analogue scale (VAS) for pain and further functional outcomes using the Majeed Pelvic Score (MPS) were recorded. In addition, computed tomography (CT) was routinely performed at 6 months postsurgery to inspect the quality of screws position. Results Excellence rate of screw position was 97% upon CT. Two patients had screws partially contacting the cortical bone but not violating sacral foramen, and no neurological symptoms were noted. All screws were secure from possible iatrogenic nerve injuries. VAS scores improved significantly over time and most patients recorded excellent functional recovery. One untoward complication occurred involving unexpected cement extravasation after sacroplasty. No associated neurologic compromise, or clinical evidence of venous emboli thrombosis was reported. Conclusion Our method aims at reducing operation time and radiation exposure to surgeons as conventional two-dimensional fluoroscopy was enough to identify safe insertion corridors in SI screw placement. Performing SI fixation in prone position is also advantageous when dealing with obese patients and concomitant spinal injuries.

title: Cryoablation for Extra-Abdominal Desmoid Tumors: a Retrospective Study of Clinical and Radiological Outcomes
container-title: Journal of vascular and interventional radiology : JVIR
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude de cohorte sur 92 séances de cryoablation chez 44 patients (*JVIR*, sept. 2026, taille médiane 6,9 cm, suivi médian 28,9 mois) rapportant 81,1 % de succès clinique, 78,4 % de réponse objective (24,3 % RC, 54,1 % RP), une concordance quasi parfaite entre volumétrie 3D et mRECIST (κ = 0,895), et seulement 5,3 % de complications majeures.

[ABSTRACT EN] Purpose To determine whether image-guided cryoablation achieves durable clinical and radiologic response with an acceptable safety profile in patients with extra-abdominal desmoid tumors and whether volumetric response assessment concords with modified Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors-based classification MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patients treated between 2020 and 2024 were identified through electronic record. Those who underwent cryoablation were included for analysis. The primary outcome was clinical success, defined as a composite of no disease progression at last follow-up, no additional treatment, and symptom improvement. The secondary outcomes included radiologic response, symptom improvement, progression-free survival, and safety. Among 208 patients diagnosed with desmoid tumors, 44 (20.7%) underwent cryoablation, of whom 38 had follow-up data available; 92 cryoablation sessions were performed. Median tumor size was 6.9 cm (interquartile range, 5.5-9.2 cm), and median follow-up duration was 28.9 months (interquartile range, 14.3-37.3 months). Results The clinical success rate was 81.1%. Radiologic response at last follow-up was complete in 24.3%, partial in 54.1%, stable in 16.2%, and progressive in 5.4% of patients. Volumetric and modified Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors-based response classification showed almost-perfect agreement (κ = 0.895). Repeat cryoablation was performed in 26.3% of patients due to radiologic progression. Additional treatment modalities were required in 13.2% of cases. The 1- and 2-year progression-free survival rates were 76.5% (95% confidence interval, 58.2%-87.6%) and 67.4% (95% confidence interval, 46.5%-81.7%), respectively. Major adverse events (Society of Interventional Radiology grade, ≥Grade 3) occurred in 5.3% of patients. Conclusions Cryoablation is a safe and effective treatment option for selected patients with extra-abdominal desmoid tumors, achieving clinical success in the majority of patients. These findings support its role in the multidisciplinary management of desmoid tumors.

title: Bipolar needle electrodes for electroporation-based treatments in soft and bone tissues: technical design and implementation
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Note technique multicentrique (*La Radiologia Medica*, sept. 2026, IF 8,9) détaillant l'architecture du champ électrique et l'implantation guidée par l'image d'électrodes aiguilles bipolaires mono-aiguille pour l'électrochimiothérapie (ECT) des tumeurs osseuses et des tissus mous, permettant de réduire le nombre d'insertions tout en confinant le champ électrique à distance des structures nerveuses.

[ABSTRACT EN] Electroporation (EP) transiently increases cell membrane permeability through the application of controlled electric pulses. Bipolar needle electrodes have been developed to simplify EP procedures by reducing the number of electrode insertions while improving control of electric field geometry and spatial confinement. This technical note describes the design principles, electric field behavior, and image-guided implementation of single-needle bipolar electrodes for EP applications in both soft and bone tissues. Electric field simulations and preclinical investigations were performed to assess field distribution, safety, and tissue selectivity. The practical implementation of the bipolar configuration is illustrated through representative image-guided examples from multiple institutions across different anatomical settings. The single-needle design enables minimally invasive procedures with predictable field control and limited extension to surrounding structures, even in anatomically complex or previously treated regions. Overall, bipolar electrodes represent a versatile and reproducible technological solution for electroporation-based treatments, supporting precise and tissue-sparing image-guided interventions.

title: Spine interventional oncology: An illustrated review of minimally invasive techniques
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Mise au point illustrée française (*Neurochirurgie*, sept. 2026, équipes Pitié-Salpêtrière & Rouen) synthétisant l'arsenal d'oncologie interventionnelle rachidienne : biopsie radioguidée, cimentoplastie des étages complexes (rachis cervical), fixation percutanée (odontoïde, sacrum, bassin), embolisation préopératoire, ablation thermique et électrochimiothérapie (ECT) en présence d'une épidurite.

[ABSTRACT EN] Spine oncological interventional radiology has become an integral component of multidisciplinary care for patients with neoplastic spinal disease. Beyond conventional vertebral augmentation, the field now encompasses image-guided biopsy, cementoplasty at complex spinal levels, percutaneous fixation, preoperative embolization of hypervascular tumors, thermal ablation, and electrochemotherapy. These techniques address complementary objectives, including histological diagnosis, rapid pain relief, mechanical stabilization, facilitation of surgery, and local tumor control in selected patients. Advances in imaging guidance, procedural planning, and device technology have enabled increasingly precise and tailored interventions in anatomically constrained regions. However, the spine remains a high-risk anatomical territory because of the proximity of the spinal cord, nerve roots, radiculomedullary arteries, and major vascular structures. Procedural safety therefore depends on careful patient selection, detailed knowledge of spinal anatomy, rigorous planning, and multidisciplinary coordination. Particularly challenging scenarios include cervical cementoplasty, percutaneous fixation of odontoid, pelvic, or sacral lesions, and tumor treatment in the presence of epidural extension. This illustrated review summarizes the main minimally invasive techniques currently used in spine interventional oncology, with emphasis on their indications, technical principles, safety strategies, limitations, and integration into contemporary oncologic care pathways.

title: Examining the current image-guided biopsy and empiric antibiotic paradigm for suspected spondylodiscitis
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude rétrospective (*Diagnostic and Interventional Radiology*, sept. 2026, IF 1,9) sur 81 biopsies disco-vertébrales guidées par l'image (62 sous TDM, 19 sous scopie) : rendement microbiologique global de 37,0 % non significativement diminué par une antibiothérapie préalable (36,4 % sous antibiotiques vs 37,8 % sans antibiotiques, p = 0,890), soulignant qu'il ne faut pas retarder l'antibiothérapie probabiliste chez un patient septique et que la biologie moléculaire (ARN 16S / NGS) est indispensable pour compléter la culture.

[ABSTRACT EN] Purpose This study aims to identify factors associated with successful pathogen isolation via percutaneous image-guided biopsy (IGB) in suspected spondylodiscitis, compare diagnostic value between fluoroscopy and computed tomography (CT) guided IGB, evaluate the influence of empiric antibiotics prior to biopsy, and assess the impact of IGB results on clinical management and patient outcomes. Methods This retrospective study examined 81 IGBs (62 CT-guided, 19 fluoroscopy-guided) performed for suspected spondylodiscitis between March 2014 and February 2025. Retrospective diagnosis was determined using a composite of biopsy microbiology, clinical criteria, and radiologic findings. Primary analyses included IGB culture yield (procedural diagnostic return), as well as sensitivity, specificity, and diagnostic accuracy. Subgroup analyses included biopsy modality and prior antibiotic administration. Results The overall culture yield was 37.0%, with a sensitivity of 44.4% and a specificity of 88.9%. Culture yield did not differ significantly among patients who received antibiotics prior to biopsy (36.4%) and those who did not (37.8%; P = 0.890). Similarly, no significant difference in yield was observed between CT-guided (38.7%) and fluoroscopic IGB (31.6%; P = 0.586). No significant difference was observed between the coaxial devices used for either transpedicular bone biopsy ( P = 0.604) or disc biopsy/aspiration ( P = 1.000). Excluding tuberculosis (TB) case, 97% of cultured organisms were susceptible to the institution's standard empiric antibiotic regimen of vancomycin and ceftriaxone. Conclusion In cases of suspected spondylodiscitis, IGB demonstrated low sensitivity and rarely altered clinical management during the study. Culture yield was not significantly diminished by prior antibiotic therapy, and 97% of cultured organisms (excluding TB) were susceptible to this institution's standard empiric antibiotics. Furthermore, the relative infrequency of positive cultures suggests that empiric antibiotic initiation should not be delayed solely for the purpose of biopsy in clinically stable patients with characteristic magnetic resonance imaging findings and elevated inflammatory markers. Although the findings in this single-center retrospective study support consideration of a more selective use of IGB, further multicenter studies and meta-analyses are warranted. Clinical significance If additional larger studies corroborate these findings, this could result in a paradigm shift for the clinical management of suspected spondylodiscitis.

title: Dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and intravoxel incoherent motion imaging for characterizing angiogenesis in soft-tissue sarcomas: an exploratory study based on MRI-pathology co-alignment
container-title: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude prospective sur 70 sarcomes des tissus mous en IRM 3T (*Quantitative Imaging in Medicine and Surgery*, nov. 2026) avec co-alignement spatial coupe-à-coupe IRM/anatomopathologie, démontrant que les paramètres Ktrans (DCE-MRI) et D* (IVIM) corrèlent fortement avec l'expression de VEGF et la densité microvasculaire (MVD) avec une AUC de 0,86.

[ABSTRACT EN] BACKGROUND: Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) expression and microvessel density (MVD) are established markers of tumor angiogenesis and key targets for anti-angiogenic therapy in soft-tissue sarcomas (STSs). Dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) and intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM) imaging are complementary magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) methods commonly used to assess angiogenesis in a variety of tumors. This study aimed to explore whether DCE-MRI and IVIM imaging could be used as non-invasive tools to evaluate tumor angiogenesis in STS based on MRI-pathology co-alignment. METHODS: In total, 70 patients with STS underwent 3.0-T DCE-MRI and IVIM imaging. The volume transfer constant (Ktrans), reflux rate constant (Kep), volume fraction of the extravascular extracellular space (Ve), true diffusion coefficient (D), pseudo-diffusion coefficient (D*), and perfusion fraction (f) were measured. Correlations between MRI parameters and VEGF expression or MVD were examined. Differences in MRI parameters between tumors with low and high VEGF expression were evaluated. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were generated, and interobserver reproducibility was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). An MRI-pathology control protocol was implemented to verify the spatial correspondence between MRI slices and their corresponding histologic sections. RESULTS: Ktrans, Kep, D*, and f were positively correlated with VEGF expression (r=0.673, 0.573, 0.692, and 0.386, respectively) and MVD (r=0.662, 0.595, 0.619, and 0.344, respectively). Ktrans and D* were identified as independent factors associated with VEGF expression and MVD. No significant correlations were observed between Ve or D and either angiogenesis marker. Tumors with high VEGF expression exhibited higher Ktrans, Kep, D*, and f values than those with low VEGF expression. The areas under the ROC curves for the four parameters in differentiating between tumors with low and high VEGF expression were 0.861, 0.844, 0.860, and 0.720, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: The study demonstrated associations between DCE-MRI- and IVIM-derived perfusion metrics and VEGF expression and MVD in STSs.

title: Mapping Genicular Nerve Endings for Optimal Pain Management: A Comparative Cadaveric Analysis Between Native Versus Prosthetic Knee
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude anatomique et histologique (*Pain Medicine*, septembre 2026 — Fonkoué et al.) cartographiant la densité des terminaisons nociceptives des nerfs géniculés dans la capsule du genou natif et prothétique afin d'affiner le positionnement des aiguilles de bloc et de radiofréquence.

[ABSTRACT EN] Background Chronic knee pain, often due to osteoarthritis (OA), is frequently treated with genicular nerve blocks, radiofrequency ablation (RFA) or genicular artery embolization (GAE). However, the intracapsular distribution of nerve endings and vascular networks key pain parameters remains poorly defined in native and prosthetic knees. Questions/purposes We compared the distribution of intracapsular nerve endings and vascular density in native versus prosthetic knee capsules across five genicular nerve targets in relation to knee pain. Methods Ten native and ten prosthetic cadaveric knees were analyzed. Capsular samples (20 × 5 mm) were harvested from regions innervated by the superior medial, superior lateral, and inferior genicular nerves, the recurrent fibular nerve, and the infrapatellar branch of the saphenous nerve. Nerve endings and vascular densities were quantified after histologic and immunohistochemical analysis comparatively. Results Native knees had higher free nerve ending (FNE) density (p Conclusion Dense FNE populations in native knees support genicular nerve-targeted interventions for OA pain. The increased vascularity and mechanoreceptor innervation identified in prosthetic knees suggest that inflammatory, angiogenic, and sensory mechanisms may contribute to persistent post-surgical pain. Whether interventions targeting these pathways, such as radiofrequency ablation or genicular artery embolization, provide better clinical benefit together remains to be established.

title: Local anesthetic selection for spine and large joint radiofrequency ablation: a practical review for the musculoskeletal radiologist
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Mise au point pratique (*Skeletal Radiology*, sept. 2026) définissant le choix, la concentration et le séquençage des anesthésiques locaux lors des procédures de radiofréquence (RFA) rachidienne (branches médiales), sacro-iliaque et des grandes articulations périphériques (genou, hanche, épaule) afin de préserver la fiabilité des tests de stimulation motrice/sensitive et d'optimiser l'analgésie.

[ABSTRACT EN] Local anesthetic (LA) selection for radiofrequency ablation (RFA) of spinal medial branch nerves, sacroiliac joint lateral branches, and large peripheral joint articular branches has not been addressed by any dedicated document. The concentration, class, and sequencing of agents used during needle placement, stimulation testing, and pre-lesioning injection have plausible implications for procedural accuracy and post-procedural analgesia. This review synthesizes pharmacological data and adjacent procedural literature into practice considerations for the musculoskeletal radiologist. No randomized or prospective comparative trial has evaluated LA agents, concentrations, or sequencing within an RFA procedure; every statement therefore rests on indirect evidence, mechanistic reasoning, or the authors' practice, and each is labeled accordingly. Lidocaine 1% is a reasonable default for skin, subcutaneous, and deep track anesthesia. Where sensory and/or motor stimulation testing is performed, there is a mechanistic argument for avoiding lidocaine 2% close to the target nerve, since selectivity between fiber classes falls as concentration rises; that argument derives from epidural quantitative sensory testing and rodent electrophysiology, has not been tested in RFA, and no study has shown that lidocaine 2% impairs stimulation testing or procedural outcome. Bupivacaine 0.25% or ropivacaine 0.2% is a reasonable choice for perineural injection before lesioning. Premixing lidocaine and bupivacaine has no demonstrated advantage: across five randomized trials, all outside interventional pain settings and heterogeneous in design, mixtures did not accelerate onset relative to bupivacaine alone and in several curtailed its duration; two also found same-site sequential injection no better than premixing. Ropivacaine is a reasonable preference in cardiac conduction disease or multi-level procedures. A structured allergy substitution pathway is provided with formal allergist evaluation as the central step. These considerations are offered to inform practice and to prompt the prospective studies the field lacks.

title: Predictors of Treatment Success After Intercostal Nerve Radiofrequency for Intercostal Neuralgia: A Retrospective
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude comparative rétrospective (*Pain Physician*, sept. 2026, IF 3,1) chez 60 adultes souffrant de névralgie intercostale post-traumatique, post-zostérienne ou idiopathique réfractaire : la radiofréquence thermique conventionnelle (CRF, n = 31) procure une analgésie nettement plus durable à 3 et 6 mois que la radiofréquence pulsée (PRF, n = 29 ; NRS à 6 mois : 2,81 ± 1,93 vs 6,31 ± 2,34, p < 0,001) et constitue le seul facteur prédictif indépendant de réponse clinique IMMPACT (OR = 9,40 ; p = 0,001).

[ABSTRACT EN] Background Intercostal neuralgia, which is characterized by neuropathic pain along the distribution of the intercostal nerves (ICNs), can impair patients' quality of life substantially. ICN-targeted radiofrequency (RF) treatment is used increasingly in current practice; however, data on factors that predict the success of such treatments remain limited. Objectives This study aims to evaluate factors associated with treatment success in patients with intercostal neuralgia who underwent ICN-targeted RF treatment. Study design A retrospective cohort study. Setting A single-center retrospective study conducted at Mersin University Faculty of Medicine Hospital. Methods This retrospective chart review included adults who had post-traumatic, postherpetic, or idiopathic intercostal neuralgia and underwent ultrasound-guided conventional radiofrequency ablation (CRF) or pulsed radiofrequency treatment (PRF) on their ICNs between January 1, 2018, and May 30, 2025. Pain intensity (measured on the NRS-11) was assessed at baseline and at 3 and 6 months after the procedure. The primary outcome was the 6-month treatment response (according to IMMPACT criteria: ≥ 50% pain reduction or a ≥ 4-point decrease in NRS score from its baseline counterpart). Group comparisons and multivariable logistic regression were performed to evaluate the outcomes and predictors of response. Results Sixty patients were included in the analysis (CRF, n = 31; PRF, n = 29). At both 3 and 6 months, mean NRS scores were significantly lower in the CRF group than in the PRF group (3 months: 2.77 ± 1.80 vs 5.83 ± 2.55; P Limitations The single-center setting, relatively small sample size, and retrospective study design. Conclusions Ultrasound-guided intercostal CRF may provide clinically meaningful analgesia for patients with refractory intercostal neuralgia. Although both modalities were associated with short-term pain improvement, CRF produced significantly more sustained pain reduction at 3 and 6 months and emerged as the sole independent predictor of treatment success.

title: Pre-Spondylectomy Radiofrequency Ablation for Spinal Chordoma: An Illustrative Case and Systematic Review of Clinical Applications and Outcomes
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Revue systématique (*Current Oncology*, sept. 2026, 13 études / 33 patients / 34 sites de chordomes rachidiens ou sacrés traités par cryoablation [n=21] ou radiofréquence [n=11]) et cas illustratif de chordome L4 traité par RFA + vertébroplastie scanoguidée avant spondylectomie en bloc, sans déficit neurologique ni récidive à 18 mois.

[ABSTRACT EN] Chordomas are rare, locally aggressive spinal tumors. En bloc resection may improve local control but can cause substantial morbidity. Thermal ablation may provide a less invasive adjunct or alternative in selected cases. We systematically reviewed reports of radiofrequency ablation (RFA), cryoablation, laser interstitial thermal therapy, high-intensity focused ultrasound, and similar thermal techniques for spinal or sacral chordoma to characterize their clinical applications and reported clinical and radiographic outcomes across pre-resection, primary non-operative, and palliative settings. Eligible studies reported at least one ablation-related clinical or radiographic outcome. Data were descriptively synthesized, and risk of bias was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute criteria. Thirteen studies including 33 patients and 34 ablated sites were identified. Cryoablation was used in 21 patients, RFA in 11 patients, and laser interstitial thermal therapy in one patient. Ablation was used as a pre-resection adjunct, primary treatment for unresectable disease, or palliation for recurrent or metastatic lesions. Most reports described pain improvement, short-term local stability, and few major complications. We also report an L4 chordoma treated with CT-guided RFA and vertebroplasty before staged en bloc spondylectomy, without a new neurologic deficit or local recurrence at 18 months. Thermal ablation may be a technically feasible adjunct, primary non-operative option, or palliative strategy for carefully selected spinal and sacral chordomas. In the presented mobile-spine case, planned pre-spondylectomy RFA was feasible before staged en bloc resection; however, limited follow-up and sparse heterogeneous literature preclude conclusions regarding long-term local control, recurrence reduction, survival, or routine use. Ablation should not replace oncologically appropriate en bloc resection when that procedure can be safely achieved and should be considered selectively within multidisciplinary chordoma care.

title: Robot-assisted targeting for osteoid osteoma: a systematic review
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Revue systématique (*Journal of Robotic Surgery*, août 2026, 12 études / 440 procédures dont 232 assistées par robot) évaluant l'apport du positionnement robotique lors du forage et de l'ablation thermique des ostéomes ostéoïdes : réduction du nombre de repositionnements de broche et fenêtres osseuses plus économiques, avec une efficacité clinique et une sécurité équivalentes au guidage TDM expert à main levée.

[ABSTRACT EN] Accurate nidus access is essential for treating osteoid osteoma, but the incremental contribution of physical robotic targeting should be distinguished from imaging, definitive treatment, and the wider care pathway. We systematically reviewed peer-reviewed human reports in which a robot physically positioned or constrained an instrument used for biopsy or treatment. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, the Cochrane Library, Wanfang Data and the China National Knowledge Infrastructure were searched from inception through August 2026, without a final language restriction. Primary outcomes were success, recurrence or retreatment, and treatment-related complications. Secondary outcomes included localization, instrument corrections, radiation, procedure time, diagnostic yield, recovery, and cost. Twelve reports contained 440 report-level treatment records, including 232 robot-assisted procedures, before assessment of probable or possible overlap. Evidence comprised seven retrospective comparisons, four uncontrolled series, and one case report. Robot-proximal findings generally favored more reproducible or conservative access, including fewer Kirschner-wire corrections, shorter localization, greater resection accuracy, or a smaller bone window. Procedure-time effects varied by comparator and workflow. In comparisons that approximately held treatment constant, clinical success, later pain, recurrence, and complications were not clearly improved. Apparent advantages over open surgery mainly reflected minimally invasive access or treatment modality rather than robotic targeting alone. Meta-analysis was not performed because clinically equivalent comparisons were not independently replicated, outcome definitions differed, and cohort overlap was probable or possible. Comparative certainty was very low. Robotic targeting may improve trajectory execution in technically demanding lesions, but superior long-term effectiveness, safety, diagnostic adequacy, robot-attributable radiation reduction, and cost-effectiveness remain unproven.

title: Avoiding pitfalls in percutaneous acetabular column screw placement using combined fluoroscopic check-point views: a technical note and case series
container-title: European journal of orthopaedic surgery & traumatology : orthopedie traumatologie
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Note technique et série clinique (*Eur J Orthop Surg Traumatol*, août 2026) décrivant trois incidences fluoroscopiques spécifiques — dont la vue combinée 'Obturator Oblique Hyper-Outlet' (COOHO) — pour démasquer les effractions corticales 'in-out-in' lors du vissage percutané des colonnes acétabulaires.

[ABSTRACT EN] Standard fluoroscopic views may not detect cortical breaches during percutaneous acetabular column screw placement, creating an illusion of safe intraosseous positioning. The purpose of this study was to illustrate use of simple fluoroscopic checkpoint projections-the combined obturator oblique hyper-outlet (COOHO) view for anterior column (AC) screws and two known additional views, outlet and true lateral (TL), for posterior column (PC) screws-as a method to demonstrate extraosseous screw trajectories that might be missed by standard tangential column fluoroscopic views. Six clinical cases are presented as examples of standard orthogonal fluoroscopic views failing to detect extraosseous screw placement. The cases are supplemented by a synthetic pelvic model demonstration to define radiographic landmarks and common screw malposition. Guidewires were advanced in the pelvic model columns, either intraosseous or extraosseous, and their paths were evaluated with standard fluoroscopic views compared to COOHO and outlet and TL views. For the AC, COOHO tangentially profiles the pectineus recess and iliopsoas gutter to unmask in-out-in paths. For the PC, iliac and obturator oblique views may miss medial or posterior breach near the lesser sciatic notch and quadrilateral plate. The outlet and TL views show the vertical extent of the ilioischial line to detect medial or posterior breech and length-orientation errors. The COOHO, outlet and TL views additional projections that improve tangential visualization of high-risk cortices and detection of extraosseous trajectories.

title: Analysis of bone metastasis multidisciplinary team meeting activity in a university hospital: patient profiles, prognostic factors
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude rétrospective de l'équipe AP-HP Pitié-Salpêtrière (*World Journal of Surgical Oncology*, août 2026, 992 dossiers / 630 patients) analysant l'activité d'une RCP Métastases Osseuses universitaire : atteinte rachidienne dans 85 % et pelvienne dans 51 % des cas, avec recours à la cimentoplastie percutanée chez 39 % des patients (contre 22 % de chirurgie).

[ABSTRACT EN] Background Bone metastases a represent a challenge in the oncological management of patients as the complications can be severe, as fractures or neurological impairment in spinal metastases. Recommendations on the management of bone metastases are constantly being improved. However, there are few recent prognostic data on bone metastases in the literature to assess the impact of advances in oncological treatment on patient survival. Hypothesis An analysis of the activity of an MDT (Multidisciplinary Team Meeting) over 2 years could provide recent data regarding prognosis of patients presenting with bone metastasis. Materials and methods This is a retrospective study of patients presented at an MDT from 2020 to 2021 in a university hospital. The objectives were to describe a representative cohort of patients with bone metastasis and the therapeutic decisions made (cementoplasty/radiotherapy/surgery) and patient survival according to tumor type, location of bone metastasis (spine/pelvis/other). Results Nine hundred ninety-two presentations of 630 patients were analyzed. The most frequent primary cancer was bronchopulmonary, followed by breast, myeloma, prostate and thyroid. 85% of patients had a spinal lesion, 51% a pelvic lesion and 52% another bone site. 49% of patients underwent radiotherapy, 39% cementoplasty and 22% surgery. Median survival was 17 months. Bronchopulmonary and prostate tumors patients had a poorer prognosis. 37% of operated patients died within 6 months of follow-up. Conclusion This study provides a description of bone MDT meeting activity in a university hospital setting, and gives a picture of the volume of activity, prognostic factors and decisions taken with significant recourse to cementoplasty, compared with older series. The presence of bone metastases still represents a turning point in the progression of oncological diseases. Level of evidence IV, retrospective study.

title: Percutaneous calcium phosphate cement injection for unicameral bone cysts: mid- to long-term clinical and radiographic outcomes
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Série clinique à long terme (*Frontiers in Surgery*, août 2026, IF 1,8, Open-Access, suivi moyen 61,1 mois jusqu'à 12 ans) chez 31 enfants et jeunes adultes porteurs d'un kyste osseux essentiel (dont 14 révélés par fracture pathologique) traités par injection percutanée de ciment phosphocalcique (CPC) : disparition complète des douleurs (EVA médiane à 0), score fonctionnel MSTS médian de 30/30, cicatrisation radiographique Neer I/II dans 100 % des cas finaux et taux de récidive primaire limité à 12,9 % (4/31).

[ABSTRACT EN] Objective Unicameral bone cysts (UBCs) are fluid-filled, osteolytic lesions commonly affecting children and adolescents. Minimally invasive treatments such as percutaneous injection have become increasingly popular. Calcium phosphate cement (CPC), a biocompatible artificial bone substitute with mechanical strength and osteoconductivity, and may be suitable for such applications. This study aimed to evaluate the mid- to long-term clinical and radiographic outcomes of percutaneous calcium phosphate cement injection for UBCs, with particular emphasis on late recurrence, repeat injection, cortical remodeling, and cavity filling. Methods A retrospective review was conducted on 31 patients with UBC treated by CPC injection between January 2013 and January 2025, with at least 1 year of follow-up. Postoperative outcomes were assessed radiographically, functionally, and for complications. We recorded the patients' age, sex, preoperative and postoperative visual analog scale (VAS) scores, Musculoskeletal Tumor Society (MSTS) scores, modified Neer classification and Capanna classification, cortical thickness ratio, cavity filling, recurrence, repeat intervention, and complications. Results The mean follow-up duration was 61.1 months (range, 13-149 months). Among them, 14 patients experienced pathological fractures. Postoperatively, pain and functional outcomes improved significantly, with the median VAS score decreasing to 0 and the median MSTS score improving to 30 at final follow-up ( P Conclusion Percutaneous CPC injection was associated with pain relief, functional improvement, and radiographic stabilization in patients with UBCs. Repeat CPC injection appeared to provide stable outcomes in recurrent cases, whereas observation was considered reasonable for one clinically stable lesion with adequate cortical thickness. The observed cortical remodeling and cavity filling suggest that CPC injection may represent a potential minimally invasive strategy for reconstruction of UBC-related bone defects.

title: Percutaneous Management of Desmoid Tumors
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Revue récente (*Current Oncology Reports*, 2026) précisant la place de la radiologie interventionnelle (cryoablation, micro-ondes, HIFU, embolisation transartérielle) dans l'algorithme moderne des tumeurs desmoïdes aux côtés de la surveillance active et des nouvelles thérapies ciblées (nirogacestat, sorafénib).

[ABSTRACT EN] Purpose of review To provide a comprehensive review of percutaneous image-guided techniques in the management of desmoid tumors including evolving thermal and non-thermal ablation options, as well as trans-arterial catheter options. Beyond each treatment modality, we aim to highlight considerations related to patient selection, technical components, and the growing interplay between percutaneous therapies and emerging systemic therapies. Recent findings Percutaneous ablation, particularly cryoablation, has emerged as a safe and effective treatment for extra-abdominal desmoid tumors, with prospective data demonstrating durable disease control and significant improvements in pain and functional status. A meta-analysis of 694 desmoid tumors treated with thermal ablation reported pooled local control of 88%, symptom relief in 90% of patients, and major complication rates below 5%. Transarterial doxorubicin-eluting embolization has shown promise in both adult and pediatric settings, while bland particle and radioembolic approaches remain under investigation. Irreversible electroporation is emerging as a non-thermal alternative near critical structures.
